newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Laura Ashley profits up, shares fall.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Laura Ashley profits up, shares fall.

text.p: British retailer Laura Ashley reported a 70 percent jump in profits on Tuesday and announced plans to expand home furnishing as part of a radical shake up under new American chief executive Ann Iverson.
But the profit recovery failed to match expectations and the retailer's shares fell steeply. They stood 22 pence lower at 192 pence at 1245 GMT.

Pretax profits rose to 5.2 million pounds ($8.1 million) from three million. Sales fell to 156.1 million pounds from 164.6 million because of a reduction in mail order and perfume activities and the sale of Australian operations last year. Underlying sales rose by 3.2 percent.
The dividend was 0.4 pence a share, the first interim payment since 1989.
But retail analysts were unimpressed. "The market had expected profits of six million pounds and a dividend of 0.5 pence," said one.

Laura Ashley, famous for its traditionally English flowery dresses and furnishings, has begun expanding its higher-margin home furnishings business in Britain and the United States as part of a three-year recovery programme.
Chief executive Ann Iverson, who took over last year, said in a statement the company's recovery was running to plan.
"The group remains on track through its shop expansion programme and its focus on improving product and gross margins, to achieve acceptable returns for shareholders over the next three years."

Iverson, who made her name in Britain by turning around Storehouse Plc's BhS and childrenswear chain Mothercare, was hired last year to revive profits as Laura Ashley was struggling to cope with financial troubles caused by over-expansion and under-investment.
The retailer is in the process of closing smaller shops and opening larger ones to display its home furnishing ranges, which have scope for bigger profits.
It plans to add more than 100,000 square feet of store space in the United States this year mainly via larger format stores, finance director Jim Walsh said in an interview.

In Britain, Laura Ashley is adding 33,000 square feet of space this year, opening 16 new stores and closing six. An out-of-town home furnishing store will open in Warrington in northwest England in November and another store is opening in Cardiff in south Wales next month, he said.
The group also plans to expand its presence in supermarket group Sainsbury's Homebase stores, where it currently has 65 outlets, Walsh said.

The group has made progress clearing out old stock and reducing costs, which fell by about six percent in the first half. Walsh said gross margins and sales were set to get a boost early next year when the first ranges from Basha Cohen, the new director of design and buying, are due to hit the shops.

But he denied that the new-look fashions and fabrics would move completely away from the Laura Ashley floral prints which turned the business from a cottage industry in the 1950s into an international brand.
"It's taking the flower and updating it," Walsh said.
